- **Routing**: customer portal on `https://BASE_DOMAIN` (admin path returns 404 here — hidden); admin ops portal on `https://ADMIN_HOST` (secret subdomain, root 302→/admin); staging on `https://STAGING_HOST`. HTTP→HTTPS 301. Real LE cert (auto-renews via certbot timer); self-signed fallback for bare-IP. A raw `http://51.79.162.96:8080` fallback listener also exists for staging (no TLS, no forwarded headers) — it's a debug path only, not how a real customer or any Server Action's origin check expects to be reached; testing against it directly produces false failures (CSP/origin-check errors) that don't reproduce on the real `STAGING_HOST`.
- Secure cookies are on (`COOKIE_SECURE=1`) now that real HTTPS exists. Stripe webhook is live at `https://BASE_DOMAIN/api/stripe/webhook`.

## Environments

- **Production**: `/opt/nxeon`, DB `nxeon`, services `nxeon-web` (port 3000) + `nxeon-worker`, nginx port 80, VPS pools IP 10.20.0.100–250 / SSH ports 20000–29999, NAT chain `NXEON_FWD`. Public: http://51.79.162.96
- **Staging**: `/opt/nxeon-staging`, DB `nxeon_staging`, services `nxeon-staging-web` (port 3001) + `nxeon-staging-worker`, nginx port 8080, ISOLATED VPS pools IP 10.20.0.50–99 / SSH ports 30000–30999, NAT chain `NXEON_FWD_STG`, VM tag `nxeon-staging`. Public: http://51.79.162.96:8080 (see the TLS note above — prefer `STAGING_HOST` over the bare port for anything that exercises real form submissions). Admin creds: `/root/nxeon-staging-credentials.txt`.
- **node-2 sandbox** (optional, not required): `nxeon-fsn1` (178.63.94.114), tree at `/opt/nxeon-v2`, its own DB (`nxeon_v2`), `NXEON_SANDBOX=1` (stubs Proxmox provisioning + Stripe charges only — everything else is real code against a real, separate DB). Useful for large or highly experimental work in isolation; not part of the normal edit→stage→promote path above. Root SSH from node-2 to this box exists (`scripts/node1.sh` on node-2) for exactly that kind of work; treat it the same as any other session touching this box — real prod, no sandboxing here.
- Instance differences are driven entirely by `.env` (NXEON_ENV, NXEON_COOKIE_NAME, NXEON_NAT_CHAIN, NXEON_TAG, NXEON_IP_START/END, NXEON_SSH_PORT_START/END, NXEON_CRED_FILE, PORT, APP_URL) — the code is identical.
- **Deploy flow**: push to GitHub → `scripts/deploy-staging.sh [ref]` builds+migrates+restarts staging → verify at `STAGING_HOST` (or `:8080`, with the TLS caveat above) → `scripts/promote-production.sh` rebuilds+restarts production. Test changes on staging before promoting — always.

## Safety rules

- NEVER touch VMIDs 9000–9999 (templates) except to add new templates.
- Staging and production share the Proxmox node but never overlap: staging only ever allocates IPs .50–.99 and ports 30000–30999. Never point staging pools at production ranges.
- Test risky/provisioning changes on staging (`scripts/deploy-staging.sh`) before promoting to production.
- Never `qm destroy` a VM that has a `Server` row — always go through a DELETE job.
- Never `pkill -f` by pattern on this box — kill by port PID or systemd unit instead (a pattern match has restarted live production before).
- Do not commit `.env`. Do not print the Proxmox token into logs or docs.
- Always `git commit` working states; never leave the tree broken — services restart from this directory.

</system-reminder>

# 15 Learning loop

Cyrus cannot fine-tune Claude. "Learning" here means **mining real build outcomes into reviewed changes** (failure rules, version-sheet facts, golden tests, routing rules, planner / guard coaching) and **shipping them as gated engine releases**. Everything below is built on branch `feature/cyrus-learning-loop`, behind `CYRUS_LEARNING` (off), not deployed. Owner decisions: [D-60 and D-61](10-decisions.md).

## Data policy (D-60)
- **Collected by default, anonymized: outcome data only.** Per build: what kind of request (fresh / change, request length bucket, planned lanes), the lane, the model tier and family, the result (success, refused, interrupted, unavailable, failed), the fixes (repairs, attempts, autofixes), turns / cost / estimated tokens per call kind, Test Flight and install outcome, and counts of what a change removed.
- **Never collected into the learning data:** user mod code, imported or third-party mods, file contents, request text, class / command / config-key names, plugin names, user ids. The export record (`lib/cyrus/learning/export.ts`) carries counts where the in-memory signals carry names; build ids are opaque Cyrus ids. The mining job quotes request text or names **only** when a staff member passes `--include-prompts` / `--include-names`, into a staff-local gitignored directory.
- **Template sharing is a separate opt-in feature** and is not part of this loop.
- Retention follows ModBuild (the loop reads ModBuild, it does not copy it anywhere else).

## The loop
1. **Signals** (`lib/cyrus/learning`, pure) derive per-build outcome facts from ModBuild rows and the stored result JSON.
2. **Report** (`scripts/cyrus/learning-report.ts`) turns signals into a token-efficiency baseline with ranked levers.
3. **Mining** (`scripts/cyrus/learning-mine.ts`) clusters failed / re-requested / regressed builds into **candidates**. It never writes to the rules, sheets, prompts or router.
4. **Review**: a person reads `review.md` (or the admin Learning tab), accepts, edits or rejects each candidate. Accepting means writing the rule / sheet fact / golden case / routing change in a normal branch with tests.
5. **Gate**: the change must pass the eval harness against the accepted baseline (`evalGate` in the release manifest module: a pass-rate drop of more than 1 point blocks).
6. **Engine release**: prompts, sheets, rules, scanner and image hashes are recorded in one **release manifest** with the eval baseline reference and a rollback pointer. The manifest module is pure and **not wired to any deploy**; deploys stay with the owner (`deploy-modbuilder.sh`, D-53).

## Signals (what each one means)
| Signal | Definition |
|---|---|
| rework | the earliest later *change* of the same lineage that builds on this build (or on its base: a discard-and-retry) starts within **30 minutes** after this build ended. Upper bound of waste: a new feature request also counts. Wasted spend = this build's cost. |
| retry | a failed / refused / interrupted build re-sent word for word by the same user within 30 minutes (compared by hash). |
| regression | the change **lost commands or sub-commands, or half or more of the classes** of its base build (**major**), or lost anything smaller (**minor**). Also computed against the **last good build** of the lineage, so a chain of small drifts is caught. A config-key loss alone is minor unless both sides come from jar listings (the stored `config` list can be shorter than the real config.yml). |
| good / kept | succeeded, not reworked, no major regression vs its base nor vs the last good build. |
| guard refusal | `errorCode: refused` (reason from `errorDetail`, e.g. `guard:injection`). |
| interruption / unavailable | `interrupted`, or `unavailable` / `unreachable` / `lost`. |
| Test Flight failure | stored verdict `failed`, a failed check, `gave_up`, or a failed stress verdict. |
| install failure | `lastInstall` with an error. **Not recorded today** (written on success only); see gaps. |
| tier vs outcome | per Katara / Saka / Yakko: builds, kept successes, re-requests, spend, cost per success and per kept success. |
| per lane | planned lanes (`cyrus.assets.planned`) or `plain`: turns, cost, estimated tokens ($0.002 each, D-03). |

Surface (classes, commands, config keys) comes from the stored result (`files`, `commands`, `config`) or, when supplied, from jar listings (`surfaceOfJar`, `yamlKeys`). The golden fixture is the owner's ChunkMirror lineage: v1.3.0 good, then the Spawner Wand build (planner turned "mob spawner" into a designer lane and the plugin's commands and five classes disappeared) and the Haiku bolt-on that never restored them.

## Scripts
| Script | What it does |
|---|---|
| `scripts/cyrus/learning-report.ts` | Read-only. One SELECT in a read-only transaction (request text hashed) or `--input rows.json`; writes the markdown report (`--out FILE`) or `--json`. |
| `scripts/cyrus/learning-mine.ts` | Same input; writes `candidates.jsonl`, `review.md`, `signals.jsonl` (anonymized), `summary.json` to `CYRUS_LEARNING_DIR` (default `./.cyrus-learning`, gitignored) or `--out DIR`. |
| `scripts/cyrus/learning-source.ts` | Shared reader (psql with `default_transaction_read_only=on`; URL from `CYRUS_DATABASE_URL`, else `DATABASE_URL`, never printed). |

Both are light and read-only, so they may run on the primary with `NODE_PATH=/opt/nxeon/node_modules /opt/nxeon/node_modules/.bin/tsx scripts/cyrus/learning-report.ts` from a worktree (never from `/opt/nxeon`). The tests run through devhost.

## Candidates
`{id, kind, title, evidence (build ids), proposedText, confidence 0-1, rationale, status: "candidate", signal}`. Kinds: `failure-rule`, `sheet-fact`, `golden-case`, `routing-rule`, `prompt-coach-gap`. Sources today: regressions (golden case "a change keeps its base's surface" + a plan-screen "keeps / replaces / removes" gap, one item per compared base), Haiku change builds that regressed on large or lane-planned plugins (routing floor), guard refusals (golden case "the guard accepts this change request" + a guard-prompt gap), Test Flight failures by check id, repair-heavy builds by lane, repeated API lookups (sheet-fact), and correction wording in a follow-up (only with `--include-prompts`). Confidence rises with the number of builds, a confirming rework, and an owner-visible loss.

## Engine release manifest
`lib/cyrus/learning/release-manifest.ts`: `{id: er-<hash of components>, status draft|canary|live|rolled-back|superseded, components {prompts base + sections, sheets name+sha256, rules version+sha256, scanner profile+sha256, image name+tag(+digest), jdk, toolchain}, evalBaseline {file, sha256, finalPassPct, builds, acceptedAt}, candidates [ids], rollback {toReleaseId, how}}`. `validateManifest` (a live / canary release needs a baseline and a rollback pointer), `diffManifests`, `evalGate`, `rollbackTarget`. It complements the per-build `EngineRelease` (`lib/cyrus/engine-core/release.ts`), which says which engine made one build; this says what an engine release *is*. Idea source: `GAPS-AND-IDEAS.md` ("treat prompt + sheets + rules + scanner + image as one engine release, canary, auto-rollback on eval regression").

## Admin tab
`/admin/cyrus/learning` (ADMIN, `fleet` area, after Storage): signals summary, outcome by tier, ranked levers, candidates with links to the build pages. Read-only (no form, no action). Without `CYRUS_LEARNING` it shows an "off" notice and reads nothing. With the flag on, `toResult` (`lib/modbuilder/store.ts`) also keeps the token usage the build service already measures (`result.ai.calls[].tokens`, `toolCalls`, `apiMs`, `explore`, `turnsDetail`); until then ModBuild has cost and turns per call but **no token counts**.

## Flags
`CYRUS_LEARNING` (default off): admin tab + usage capture. `CYRUS_LEARNING_DIR`: where the job output is read from. The scripts run without the flag.

## Baseline of 2026-10-12 (27 builds, all the owner's; $6.51)
Full report: `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-research/BJ-token-efficiency-baseline.md`. 24 of 27 succeeded, 18 were kept; $1.47 (23% of spend) went on four builds the owner followed with another change within 30 minutes; Saka was 47% of spend (cost per kept success $0.77 against Katara $0.17); the Haiku 18-turn change build (`mb3445257a`) cost $0.21 and dropped the commands and all five classes of the last good build. Top levers (estimates, see the report for assumptions): Saka on Sonnet 5.5, a regression guard on change builds, several edits per response, medium effort, fewer re-requests via a "what stays, what goes" check.

## What is not verified
- All numbers come from 27 builds; token savings are estimates (no token counts stored before `CYRUS_LEARNING`).
- The mining job has only ever run on the fixture and the owner's builds; no candidate has been accepted, so the review-to-release path is untested end to end.
- Install failures, player reports and "kept using it" are not recorded; the 30-minute window is the only quality signal for successes.
- Nothing was run against a live build service, a deploy, or a real eval run.

#!/bin/bash
# (Re)create the Mod Builder container on the build VM. Idempotent.
#   AUTH, one source of truth. Preferred: ONE Claude login session file (what `claude login` writes to
#   ~/.claude/.credentials.json: access token + refresh token). Keep it in a dedicated directory,
#   CLAUDE_CREDENTIALS_DIR (default /root/.claude-modbuilder), created once with
#     CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=/root/.claude-modbuilder claude login
#   (or copy an existing .credentials.json into it). The directory is mounted read-write at /run/claude-auth (CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR),
#   outside the CLI user's home and denied to the model's tools, so token refreshes persist and nothing else shares that login. When that file exists the
#   CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN line in claudebox.env is ignored (an env token would override the file).
#   WHERE TO EDIT (on the VM): /root/claudebox.env, one KEY=VALUE per line. Any ONE of: CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN (subscription),
#   ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (paid API), ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN (gateway bearer). Optional gateway: ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=https://host/v1,
#   EXTRA_ALLOWED_DOMAINS=host (the container firewall blocks everything else), MB_MODEL_PREFIX=cc/ (if the gateway namespaces models).
#   Then run this script again to restart the container.
#   Fallback (old way): /root/claudebox.env   CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN=... (owner subscription)  -- or ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=... for paid API
#   /root/modbuilder.env  MODBUILDER_API_KEY=...      (bearer key the portal uses)
set -euo pipefail
IMAGE="${1:-modbuilder:0.5}"
# Routing / knowledge knobs (see route.js, prompts.js): passed through when set in the caller's env,
# e.g. MB_ROUTING=off /opt/modbuilder/run.sh modbuilder:0.3  (or put them in /root/modbuilder.env).
PASS=()
for k in MB_ROUTING MB_CLASSIFIER MB_MODEL_SIMPLE MB_MODEL_STANDARD MB_MODEL_COMPLEX MB_REPAIR_MODEL MB_REPAIR_CHEAP_MODEL MB_REPAIR_CHEAP_FIRST MB_REPAIR_SMALL_MAX MB_ROUTE_SIMPLE_MAX MB_ROUTE_COMPLEX_MIN MB_SHEETS MB_RULES MB_MAX_REPAIRS MB_LIVE_STREAM MB_MAX_TURNS MB_MAX_TURNS_REPAIR MB_AUTOFIX MB_LEAN_TOOLS MB_EFFORT MB_CACHE_TTL MB_DEDUPE MB_DEDUPE_MAX_AGE_H MB_TIER_KATARA MB_TIER_SAKA MB_TIER_YAKKO; do
  if [[ -n "${!k:-}" ]]; then PASS+=(-e "$k=${!k}"); fi
done

#!/bin/bash
# Deploy the Cyrus build service (services/modbuilder) to the build VM 88001 and rebuild its image. OWNER RUNS THIS
# (on the primary). Agents never run it. Runbook: docs/CYRUS-DEPLOY-RUNBOOK.md step 3.
#
# The file list is DERIVED FROM THE DOCKERFILE (every COPY source), so a new module can never be forgotten here
# (test/modbuilder-dockerfile.test.ts checks `--list` against the Dockerfile). The two optional data files come from lib/.
#
#   bash scripts/cyrus/deploy-modbuilder.sh --list                 print what would be copied, touch nothing
#   bash scripts/cyrus/deploy-modbuilder.sh                         copy, build TAG, restart, health + guard smoke
#   JDK25=yes bash scripts/cyrus/deploy-modbuilder.sh               also install JDK 25 + Gradle 9 + the 26.x classpaths
#   API_KEY=sk-ant-... bash scripts/cyrus/deploy-modbuilder.sh      switch the CLI from the subscription login to an API key
#   FLIP=yes ...                                                    open the studio (launch pair) after the smoke, ONLY if /health auth=api_key
# Env: S (service dir, default: this repo), LIBDIR (lib/cyrus of the same tree), TAG (new image, default modbuilder:0.6),
#      MC26_PINS (with JDK25=yes), V/JUMP (VM + jump host).
set -uo pipefail
HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
S=${S:-$HERE/../../services/modbuilder}
LIBDIR=${LIBDIR:-$HERE/../../lib/cyrus}
TAG=${TAG:-modbuilder:0.6}
API_KEY="${API_KEY:-}"
FLIP="${FLIP:-no}"
JDK25="${JDK25:-no}"
MC26_PINS="${MC26_PINS:-26.2=26.2.build.133-stable 26.1.2=26.1.2.build.74-stable}"
V=${V:-root@10.20.1.253}
JUMP=${JUMP:-root@178.63.94.114}
SSH="ssh -o BatchMode=yes -J $JUMP"

# Every COPY source of the Dockerfile (optional globs like registry.jso[n] are skipped: they come from LIBDIR below).
files_from_dockerfile() {
  awk '/^COPY /{ n=0; for (i=2;i<NF;i++) { if ($i ~ /^--/) continue; print $i } }' "$S/Dockerfile" | grep -v '\[' | sort -u
}
FILES=$(files_from_dockerfile)
EXTRA="run.sh Dockerfile"
if [ "${1:-}" = "--list" ]; then
  for f in $FILES $EXTRA; do echo "$f"; done
  echo "lib:versions/registry.json"; echo "lib:import/deps.json"
  exit 0
fi
cd "$S" || { echo "no service dir $S"; exit 1; }
missing=""; for f in $FILES $EXTRA; do [ -e "$f" ] || missing="$missing $f"; done
# toolchain.tgz is not in git: it must already sit in /opt/modbuilder on the VM (pinned Temurin 21 + Gradle 8).
missing=$(echo "$missing" | tr ' ' '\n' | grep -v '^toolchain.tgz$' | tr '\n' ' ')
[ -z "${missing// /}" ] || { echo "missing in $S:$missing"; exit 1; }
EXPECT_PROMPT=$(sed -n 's/^const PROMPT_VERSION = "\(mb-[0-9.-]*\)";.*/\1/p' prompts.js)
[ -n "$EXPECT_PROMPT" ] || { echo "cannot read PROMPT_VERSION from prompts.js"; exit 1; }

echo "== 1/7 service must be idle"
H=$($SSH $V 'curl -s 127.0.0.1:7340/health') || { echo "cannot reach the VM"; exit 1; }
echo "$H" | cut -c1-160
echo "$H" | grep -q '"running":0' || { echo "A build is running. Run this again in a minute."; exit 1; }
PREV=$($SSH $V "docker inspect -f '{{.Config.Image}}' modbuilder" 2>/dev/null)
[ -n "$PREV" ] || { echo "cannot read the running image"; exit 1; }
echo "running image: $PREV  -> new: $TAG  (expect promptVersion $EXPECT_PROMPT)"
$SSH $V "test -f /opt/modbuilder/toolchain.tgz" || { echo "/opt/modbuilder/toolchain.tgz is missing on the VM"; exit 1; }

echo "== 2/7 backup (app files + env) and copy"
TS=$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)
BK=/opt/modbuilder/.backup-$TS.tgz
$SSH $V "cd /opt/modbuilder && tar czf $BK --exclude=toolchain.tgz --exclude='.backup-*' . /root/claudebox.env 2>/dev/null; test -s $BK" || { echo "backup failed"; exit 1; }
echo "backup: $BK (restore: tar xzf $BK -C /opt/modbuilder; cp the claudebox.env inside back to /root)"
# shellcheck disable=SC2086
tar -C "$S" -cf - $(for f in $FILES $EXTRA; do [ -e "$f" ] && echo "$f"; done) | $SSH $V 'tar -C /opt/modbuilder -xf -' || exit 1
scp -o BatchMode=yes -o ProxyJump=$JUMP "$LIBDIR/versions/registry.json" "$LIBDIR/import/deps.json" $V:/opt/modbuilder/ || exit 1

if [ -n "$API_KEY" ]; then
  echo "== 3/7 switching auth to the API key (old env kept as claudebox.env.bak-subscription; the login dir is moved aside)"
  $SSH $V "cp -a /root/claudebox.env /root/claudebox.env.bak-subscription && sed -i '/^CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN=/d;/^ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=/d' /root/claudebox.env && echo 'ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=$API_KEY' >> /root/claudebox.env && if [ -f /root/.claude-modbuilder/.credentials.json ]; then mv /root/.claude-modbuilder /root/.claude-modbuilder.bak-$TS; fi" || exit 1
else
  echo "== 3/7 auth unchanged (the current login stays)"
fi

echo "== 4/7 build $TAG and restart (a few minutes; JDK25=$JDK25)"
ARGS=""
if [ "$JDK25" = "yes" ]; then
  ARGS="--build-arg JDK25_URL=https://github.com/adoptium/temurin25-binaries/releases/download/jdk-25.0.4.1%2B1/OpenJDK25U-jdk_x64_linux_hotspot_25.0.4.1_1.tar.gz --build-arg JDK25_SHA256=dbb698396d478e7fa2b1e50f4103324b2a99b90569ee27c33f2261f9215cf41e --build-arg GRADLE9_URL=https://services.gradle.org/distributions/gradle-9.8.1-bin.zip --build-arg GRADLE9_SHA256=dce76f55f8e251a3a1f130eb120f30b3d271de2b76c9b0729d316b5a1b6dc01f"
fi
rollback() {
  echo "ROLLING BACK to $PREV (files + env from $BK)"
  $SSH $V "cd /opt/modbuilder && tar xzf $BK -C /opt/modbuilder --exclude=root/claudebox.env && tar xzf $BK -C / root/claudebox.env 2>/dev/null; if [ -d /root/.claude-modbuilder.bak-$TS ]; then rm -rf /root/.claude-modbuilder && mv /root/.claude-modbuilder.bak-$TS /root/.claude-modbuilder; fi; ./run.sh $PREV; sleep 8; curl -s 127.0.0.1:7340/health | cut -c1-160; docker logs --tail 15 modbuilder 2>&1 | tail -15"
}

input.title: Fix NxPerf first-boot config read in AI builds
input.tldr: While flying the new starter-bank mods I found that the injected perf watchdog reads the plugin config before the plugin saves its config.yml, so on a fresh install every getConfig().getX("key", fallback) returns the fallback instead of the config.yml value until the next restart. A new session would fix the watchdog and add a flight check.
input.prompt:
Bug in the Cyrus build service perf layer (services/modbuilder/perf.js + perf/src/NxPerf.java), found 2026-10-13 on branch feature/cyrus-recipe-memory while Test-Flighting starter bank mods.

perf.js patchMain() inserts `<pkg>.nxperf.NxPerf.init(this);` as the FIRST statement of onEnable. NxPerf.init -> readSettings() calls plugin.getConfig(). On a fresh server the plugin's config.yml does not exist yet, so Bukkit loads an EMPTY config (jar config.yml only as defaults) and caches it. The plugin's own saveDefaultConfig() that follows writes the file but the cached in-memory config stays empty. Bukkit's getString/getInt(path, def) with an explicit def IGNORES the defaults, so every read with a fallback returns the fallback on the first boot (nested sections come back as empty created sections). Real evidence: starter bank flight on Paper 1.21.11 (node-2) printed "No kits." and empty /discord text until the bank sources added reloadConfig() after saveDefaultConfig().

Fix suggestion (work in a NEW worktree from main, never /opt/nxeon; heavy commands via /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost): in NxPerf.init, before readSettings(), do `try { if (plugin.getResource("config.yml") != null) plugin.saveDefaultConfig(); } catch (RuntimeException ignored) {}` so the file exists before the first getConfig(), OR have patchMain insert the init call after an existing saveDefaultConfig() line. Bump PERF_VERSION, add a unit test in test/modbuilder-*.test.ts and a Test Flight RCON check (a golden that prints a nested config value on first boot). This changes every AI build, so it needs the build-service image redeploy (owner) and should be noted in docs/cyrus/02-engine.md.

## Mod lifecycle
`lib/cyrus/lifecycle` + worker sweeps: install plans, on/off, broken/outdated detection (`cyrus-compat-watch`), updates, creator warnings. Game-version rules come from `GameSupport`.

## Learning loop
`lib/cyrus/learning`: outcome signals, token levers, candidate mining and the engine release manifest, all pure and inert; scripts `scripts/cyrus/learning-report.ts` / `learning-mine.ts`; admin tab `/admin/cyrus/learning`; flag `CYRUS_LEARNING` (off). Details: [15 learning loop](15-learning-loop.md).

## Eval harness
`lib/cyrus/eval`, `scripts/cyrus/eval-run.ts`, `services/modbuilder/eval/`: 178 prompts in categories with a per-version matrix and scoring spec; one-command runner with dry run, budget cap (required for a real run), resume, stage scoring, `baseline.json` + `report.md`. First run planned: 90 builds on 1.21.11 at Saka tier, estimated $9.73-$22.23. **No paid run has happened**; tested only against a fake CLI. See [09 testing](09-testing-and-verification.md).

## Mod planner, capability catalogue and the plan screen (live-test fixes, 2026-10-11)
The first real production test (a golem that throws rocks and grunts, Yakko, 1.21.11) built plain code: assets were only requested by literal phrases. Now:
- **Planner** (`lib/cyrus/planner`): `POST /api/cyrus/plan` asks the build service's `POST /plan` (one Haiku turn, no tools, no thinking, ~$0.001, 9 s budget; service image 0.6 `features.planner`) which LANES the prompt implies (`lanes.ts`: textures, item states, sounds, 3D, creature, item/menu/quest/boss/HUD designers, motion, config, data pack, worldgen, library). The answer is validated with zod; on any failure, timeout or invalid JSON the deterministic rules (`rules.ts`) answer, and a literal ask ("custom texture") is never dropped. Golden set: `test/fixtures/cyrus-planner/golden.json` (40 prompts, 40/40 on the rules); eval hook `lib/cyrus/planner/eval.ts` + `scripts/cyrus/planner-eval.ts` (178-prompt eval set: rules recall 0.93).
- **Capability catalogue** (`lib/cyrus/adapters/capabilities.ts`, schema `cyrus.capabilities.v1`): per game, per lane: availability, reason, substitute, minimum version, required version capability (with a fallback) and host switch. Every adapter provides one (`GameAdapter.capabilities`; Minecraft: `minecraft-capabilities.ts`); beta+ needs a complete one (onboarding health `capability_catalogue`). The router (`decide.ts`) intersects the planner's needs with it, the plan tier (`asset-gate.ts`) and the switches: build / skip / blocked with a plain warning ("Creature model are not available on Minecraft 1.21.11: ... Mob skin: coming soon ... Pick 26.1.2 or newer").
- **Plan screen** (`components/cyrus/prompt/PlanSheet.tsx`, the new-mod flow): what will be created, what cannot be built and why, toggles, cost/time/tokens per model for the lanes really built, the Auto model. A plan with a blocked lane needs "Continue anyway": `createModBuild` runs `preBuildCheck` BEFORE the token hold (`requirePlanAck` from the Forge; API callers get the warnings as notices). The approved lanes go to the build as `assets: { plan: 1, lanes }` (the server rebuilds the flags from the lane list) and, on service 0.6, as `assets.plan` lines the model must produce. Entry points without a plan screen get the deterministic plan automatically.
- **Honesty**: `lib/cyrus/assets/truth.ts` lists what the build REALLY shipped in the notes ("No custom audio in this build: it uses vanilla sounds"); the service prompt says assets are optional and how to build a creature on 1.21.x (vanilla base mob + scale, custom sounds, a custom-textured thrown item).
- **Live token meter**: the service keeps `live` (per-turn usage while a call streams; `features.liveUsage`), the portal stores it as `result.live`, `lib/cyrus/tokens/spend.ts liveEstimate` shows it ("from live AI usage") or a labelled stage+time estimate on older images; the meter shows stage, elapsed time and "spent more than held". E2E: `test/cyrus-live-usage-e2e.test.ts` (real service, fake CLI `scripts/cyrus/live-usage-fake-cli.js`).
- **Holds and Auto**: `holdRange` holds the planned estimate in tokens (+20%), the reserve table is the floor; "Auto" (default) = cheapest capable model (`planner/estimate.ts autoModel`). `scripts/cyrus/pricing-table.ts` prints cost per build type per model.
- **Versions**: `components/cyrus/prompt/VersionPicker.tsx` (accessible listbox, previews disabled with the reason, "Match my server") and `GET /api/cyrus/capabilities` ("what this version supports", also on the project page).
## Minecraft coverage (bundle mc-coverage)
## Golden corpus (bundle mc-coverage)
`services/modbuilder/golden/` holds the reference plugins and anti-patterns; `node services/modbuilder/golden/harness.js` (via `scripts/devhost run --lock`) compiles + scans them like a generated build on all four versions, `--antipatterns` records which layer catches each mistake, `scripts/cyrus/golden-flight.ts fly <version>` boots them, `... results` writes `golden/results.json`. Tests: `test/cyrus-mc-coverage*.test.ts`. The coverage eval set (`eval/sets/coverage.jsonl`, 103 prompts with `expectLanes`) adds lane-selection accuracy to the runner report (`lib/cyrus/eval/lanes.ts`; rules selector baseline: exact 70.9%, recall 35.4%: the planner's job) and the `coverage-first` preset (40 builds).

## Learning loop tests (2026-10-12)
`test/cyrus-learning-signals.test.ts`, `-mining`, `-scripts`, `-admin` (about 45 cases, no AI, no network): signals on the 27 real production rows (`test/fixtures/cyrus-learning`, request text hashed, Java paths only) with the ChunkMirror lineage as the golden case, rework / retry windows, regression severity, anonymized export leak check, levers, candidate mining (deterministic ids, JSONL round trip, no names by default), release manifest (id, validation, diff, eval gate, rollback), both scripts end to end on `--input`, read-only SQL check, admin tab gate. See [15 learning loop](15-learning-loop.md).

## Eval harness and baseline (r33)
178 prompts, `scripts/cyrus/eval-run.ts` (dry run, required budget, resume, stage scoring, `baseline.json`, `report.md`). First planned run: 90 builds on 1.21.11 at Saka tier, estimated $9.73-$22.23 (asset/designer builds may cost more; unchecked whether VM 88001's image accepts tier/assets). **No paid run has happened.** Pass-rate page `/mods/cyrus/pass-rates` shows its empty state until a baseline is accepted. Older harness: 28 prompts, 28/28 built, 13/13 loaded on v6.

## Eval journal statistics (2026-10-13, first-pass reliability)
`scripts/cyrus/eval-journal-stats.ts <journal.jsonl | run dir> [--builds DIR] [--compare <baseline run>] [--json]` prints pass@1, final / full pass, the share of spend that went to builds that needed a model repair, cost p50/p80/p90 per lane and the top repair triggers (repairs / builds), so the next run proves or disproves an improvement. Logic is `lib/cyrus/eval/stats.ts` (pure, tested in `test/modbuilder-first-pass.test.ts`). Triggers come from the service record (events + `precheck` rules); runner results written since this change carry `triggers`, older journals take `--builds <dir of <id>/build.json>` copied read-only from the service. Re-run on first1 (64 builds incl. the resumed ones): pass@1 57.8%, 26 repaired builds (40.6%) = 65.4% of spend, a repaired build costs 2.7x a clean one; triggers No design found 7, perf-spawn-in-loop 7, Sound check problems 6, compile errors 4, Design check 3, Asset check 2, perf-block-loop 1, perf-raw-timer 1, Texture check 1. Compare a later run with `--compare /root/cyrus-eval/first1`.

| r39 | customer app + landing motion fix [AJ] | 10-11 07:05 |
| landing | cyrus.my live: Cloudflare zone active, nginx static v7 landing, Let's Encrypt cert issued by the watcher | 10-11 |

## Phase 2: in flight at the time of writing (2026-10-11)
These branches exist; check `git log` in their worktrees (`/tank/dev-worktrees/cyrus-r41` ...) and mark landed here when merged.
| Branch | Scope | State when this page was written |
|---|---|---|
| r41 `feature/cyrus-r41-sepux` [AL] | separation UX: Cyrus opens full screen with a slim "Back to Nxeon" strip, no Cyrus chip in the Nxeon bar, white/black Cyrus pill; v7 plan sigils (wave / flame / arcane) as the plan icons; live token meter and per-mod / per-version / per-asset spend; token rules: plan tokens roll over while active, lapse = freeze then expire (placeholder), free server tokens with scope, per-server cap, refund and early-delete reversal via Nxeon `server.purchased/renewed/refunded` events | **DONE on its branch, not merged, not deployed**, all numbers are placeholders pending OWNER-ACTIONS "r41"; tests `cyrus-sepux-r41` + DB `cyrus-tokens-r41-db` 8/8; 18 `sep-*.png` shots |
| r42 `feature/cyrus-r42-mcref` [AM] | private distilled Minecraft reference index (ids and defaults used only to validate Cyrus's assumptions) + bring-your-own game assets; the report lists where Cyrus's assumptions match or differ (details deliberately not reproduced here) | commits on branch, **not merged** |
| r43 `feature/cyrus-r43-dbmove` | moved the 338 Cyrus-table call sites outside `lib/cyrus` to `cyrusDb` (app/api, app/dashboard, app/admin + components, lib, worker + scripts); ratchet baseline now empty | **merged into r2** (338 -> 0) |
| r44 `feature/cyrus-r44-gaps` | bridge gaps (first: personal API keys accepted by API v1) | 1 commit, **not merged** |
| r45 `feature/cyrus-r45-structure` | mod structure: capability manifest, forge sub-branches, modules in one mod, ModSpec v2 (design `v8-structure/STRUCTURE-PLAN.md`, flag `CYRUS_MOD_SUITES`) | launched, design written, **not merged** |
17. **Storage (r51)**: card add-ons not run against Stripe (wallet path tested on Postgres); GB changes on a card add-on = cancel and buy again; revision/asset history is never offered for cleanup; the nightly storage report, alert rules and the admin host are not installed; prices and quotas are placeholders.
18. **Warn, don't block (D-62, branch `feature/cyrus-warn-dont-block`)**: still enforced as before and soft by policy (the "soften next" rows of `lib/cyrus/limits/inventory.ts`): designer text lengths, motion preset knobs, shop price ceilings and max active quests, data pack tick-function perf caps, worldgen counts / attempts / cost ceiling, sound set sizes and per-role lengths, texture sizes and palettes, the model-studio viewport budget. Two touch customer servers and wait for the owner: the Test Flight stress Install block (`CYRUS_PERF_BLOCK_ON_FAIL`) and the post-install watch default action (`CYRUS_PERF_WATCH_ACTION=disable`). Not verified: a real Paper server loading a generated plugin with an out-of-range value (the loader logic ran under javac + java with a stub config only), the studio UI in a browser.

18. **Prompt coach** (branch `feature/cyrus-prompt-coach`): scores and questions are word rules tuned on the golden set and the eval prompts, never measured against real customer prompts or build outcomes; the one-call rewrite never ran against the real model (fakes only; needs the build-service image with `coach.js`); the panel was not opened in a real browser or screenshotted; the customer-app New mod flow does not show it; `CyrusCoachEvent` SQL not applied.
12. **Learning loop (2026-10-12, unmerged):** token counts are not stored in ModBuild (the portal's `toResult` drops them; captured only with `CYRUS_LEARNING` on, new builds); no compiler / repair error text, install failure, player report or "kept using it" signal is stored; the mining job has run only on 27 owner builds and no candidate has gone through review, eval gate and release; the engine release manifest is not wired to any deploy; token-lever savings are estimates with stated assumptions ([15 learning loop](15-learning-loop.md)).

- Portals (2026-10-13): Live and Economy tabs and featured mods are unit-tested only; no browser run, no screenshots, no real Anthropic Admin API call (`ANTHROPIC_ADMIN_API_KEY` unset), margin preview not compared with real Stripe payouts. The Live feed shows a running build's cost from the build service's estimate and a stored copy lags until someone syncs. Featured landing section needs a landing publish by the owner. cyrus.my proxying is prepared in [CYRUS-MY-LAUNCH](CYRUS-MY-LAUNCH.md), nothing applied. One-prompt flow gaps are listed in [06 portals](06-portals.md).

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.
